data.title: The B2B Commerce Trends & Opportunities Report
data.subtitle: We sat down with B2B commerce leaders across seven firms and asked what is changing on the ground. The result is a clear-eyed look at how manufacturers, distributors, and regulated sellers are modernizing without disrupting the operations that made them successful.
bullets: Seven expert interviews. One industry in transition. System integrators, digital agencies, and technology providers describing the same shift from different angles, so you see the trending patterns.
Data readiness and ERP-connected commerce. Why clean, structured data is becoming the foundation everything else is built on, and what happens to projects that skip it.
Modernizing under private equity pressure. How teams replace legacy systems and move faster than the organization is comfortable with, without breaking the business.
Industry-specific commerce. What changes when you sell into healthcare, fintech, manufacturing, and distribution, where the catalog is the easy part.
Agentic AI and the future of B2B buying. Why buyers arrive to solve a problem under time pressure, and how conversational and visual configuration meets them there.
Practical questions for your own team. Each chapter closes with the questions worth asking before your next platform, data, or AI decision.
data.authors: Presented by Shopware. Researched and written by Content Cucumber. Featuring Matt Harris (Harris Digital), Jason Parrish (Altus Nova), Bob Lewis, Swamy Mahesh and Sidney Gallaway (impaqX), Ryan Bloms (Codal), Shae Inglis (Acro Commerce), Brendan Cameron (Americaneagle.com), and Justin Scott (Dopple).

data.alt: Ready for the New Era of B2B Commerce? Expert insights on how to modernize without disrupting the operational realities that make your business successful. Download the free B2B Commerce Trends & Opportunities Report, presented by Shopware.

data.title: B2B commerce stopped being a slower version of B2C
data.subtitle: Four through-lines the contributors kept returning to, no matter which sector they work in.

items.title: Operational complexity keeps increasing.
items.text: Catalogs keep growing, ERP systems keep straining, and data stays fragmented across tools that were never meant to talk to each other. The leaders in this report agree the hard part is no longer the storefront, it is the operational infrastructure underneath it.

items.title: Flexibility beats rigid feature checklists.
items.text: The teams getting modernization right align systems to how the business runs, rather than chasing the longest feature list, which is why two companies in the same industry often need different builds.

items.title: Clean, structured data is becoming the foundation.
items.text: Every contributor circled back to data readiness. AI, search, automation, and customer support all sit on top of it, and the projects that skip it pay for it later in ways that are hard to see until they hurt.

items.title: Buyers arrive with a problem to solve.
items.text: Contractors, technicians, and procurement teams arrive under time pressure trying to get one specific thing done. That is pushing demand toward contextual, conversational, and visual commerce, and away from the catalog grid.
